    seq = reference[row['transcript']].seq[row['chromStart']:row['chromEnd']]
    if row.get('strand') == '-':
        seq = seq.reverse_complement()

    record = SeqRecord(
        Seq(str(seq)),
        id=f"{row['name']}_{row['repeats']}",
        description=f"{row['transcript']}:{row['chromStart']}-{row['chromEnd']}"
    )
    records.append(record)

SeqIO.write(records, "../../data/gt_IS_nc_new.fasta", "fasta")

def collect_coords(genome, target_db, label):
    rows = []
    with Pipeline(target_db=target_db) as pipeline:
        for locus in pipeline(genome):
            target = locus.targets[0] if locus.targets else None
            num_segments = len(target.segments) if target else 0

            # Extract each segment's coordinates separately
            if target:
                for seg in target.segments:
                    rows.append({
                        "label":        label,
                        "locus_id":     locus.id,
                        "target":       target.id,
                        "is_stitched":  num_segments > 1,
                        "contig":       seg.contig,
                        "seg_start":    seg.start,
                        "seg_end":      seg.end,
                        "strand":       seg.strand,
                        "seg_length":   seg.end - seg.start,
                    })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def intersect_loc(df1, df2, buffer):
    hits = 0
    matched = []
    
    for _, r1 in df1.iterrows():
        for _, r2 in df2.iterrows():
            if r1["transcript"] != r2["transcript"]:
                continue
            # Check if positions overlap with buffer
            if (r1["chromStart"] - buffer) <= r2["chromEnd"] and (r1["chromEnd"] + buffer) >= r2["chromStart"]:
                hits += 1
                matched.append({
                    "transcript": r1["transcript"],
                    "start_1":   r1["chromStart"],
                    "end_1":     r1["chromEnd"],
                    "start_2":   r2["chromStart"],
                    "end_2":     r2["chromEnd"],
                    "buffer":    buffer,

    return hits, pd.DataFrame(matched)

Each is done without and with synonyms. With synonyms, names that ISfinder lists as synonyms/isoforms (e.g. IS30 / IS30D) count as the same IS, so a different name for the same element is not counted as a miss.

from eris.synonyms import SynonymResolver, fetch_isfinder_table

synonyms = SynonymResolver(fetch_isfinder_table())
loci = pd.read_csv("../result/new_merge_id/new_merge_id_report.tsv", sep="\t").drop_duplicates("locus_id")
truth = pd.read_csv("../../data/ec958_IS.reannotated.sorted.bed", sep="\t", header=None)[3]
truth = truth[truth.str.split("_").str[0] != "ISSen10"]  # ISSen10 excluded from the truth set

def is_name(name, use_synonyms):
    # IS1A_IS1_unknown_stitched / IS1A_2 -> IS1A; with synonyms, every synonym gets the same name
    return (synonyms.canonical(name) if use_synonyms else name).split("_")[0]

def copies_per_is(use_synonyms):
    eris = loci.groupby(loci["target"].map(lambda n: is_name(n, use_synonyms)))["copy_number"].sum()
    real = truth.map(lambda n: is_name(n, use_synonyms)).value_counts()
    return pd.concat([real.rename("truth"), eris.rename("eris")], axis=1).fillna(0).astype(int)

Fragmentation of the complete genome assembly from the fasta file
I want to try create a fragmentations of the complete genome assembly to see if it can improve the results. As the complete genome assembly has 3 sequences, I will try to create 150 fragments for each sequence.

# Create fragments of the complete genome assembly
from Bio import SeqIO
from Bio.SeqRecord import SeqRecord
import random

complete_fasta = "../../data/EC958_complete_genome.fasta"
fragmented_fasta = "../../data/EC958_complete_genome_fragmented.fasta"

def fragment_genome(input_fasta: str, output_fasta: str, num_fragments: int = 150):
    records = list(SeqIO.parse(input_fasta, "fasta"))
    fragments = []
    
    for record in records:
        seq_length = len(record.seq)
        fragment_size = seq_length // num_fragments
        
        for i in range(num_fragments):
            start = i * fragment_size
            end = (i + 1) * fragment_size if i < num_fragments - 1 else seq_length
            fragment_seq = record.seq[start:end]
            fragment_id = f"{record.id}_fragment_{i+1}"
            fragments.append(SeqRecord(fragment_seq, id=fragment_id, description=""))
    
    SeqIO.write(fragments, output_fasta, "fasta")
    print(f"Written {len(fragments)} fragments to {output_fasta}")


# Fragment the complete genome assembly

import pandas as pd
from collections import Counter
import IS_dict as isd

_, synonym_to_name = isd.build_synonym_dicts(isd.load_is_table())


def precision_recall(report_file, bed_file):
    # Predicted: one copy per locus; Truth: one copy per BED line
    loci = pd.read_csv(report_file, sep="\t").drop_duplicates("locus_id")
    pred_names = [n for t in loci["target"] for n in t.split(",")]
    truth_names = pd.read_csv(bed_file, sep="\t", header=None)[3]

    def clean(name):
        name = name.split("_")[0]                  # ISEc12_1 / ISEc12_IS21_unknown -> ISEc12
        return synonym_to_name.get(name, name)     # synonym -> canonical name

    pred = Counter(clean(n) for n in pred_names)
    truth = Counter(clean(n) for n in truth_names)

    rows = []
    for count_copies in (True, False):
        p, t = (pred, truth) if count_copies else (Counter(set(pred)), Counter(set(truth)))
        names = set(p) | set(t)
        tp = sum(min(p[n], t[n]) for n in names)
        fp = sum(max(0, p[n] - t[n]) for n in names)
        fn = sum(max(0, t[n] - p[n]) for n in names)
        precision = tp / (tp + fp)
        recall = tp / (tp + fn)
        rows.append({
            "Report": report_file.split("/")[-1].removesuffix("_report.tsv"),

# Create new columns based on the different postion of IS
def label_is(df, is_col="IS_name", locus_col="locus_id", synonym_lookup=None):
    """
    Adds 'canonical_IS' and 'IS_label' columns.
    Rows with the same IS name AND same locus_id get the same label (e.g. IS1_1).
    A new locus_id under the same canonical IS name gets the next number (IS1_2, IS1_3...).
    """
    df = df.copy()

    # canonicalize synonyms first, if you have a lookup
    if synonym_lookup is not None:
        df["canonical_IS"] = df[is_col].map(lambda x: synonym_lookup.get(x, x))
    else:
        df["canonical_IS"] = df[is_col]

    # rank locus_ids by first appearance, within each canonical_IS group
    def assign_labels(group):
        # order of first appearance of each locus_id within this IS group
        first_seen = group[locus_col].drop_duplicates()
        locus_to_num = {loc: i + 1 for i, loc in enumerate(first_seen)}
        group["IS_label"] = str(group.name) + "_" + group[locus_col].map(locus_to_num).astype(str)
        return group

    df = df.groupby("canonical_IS", group_keys=False, sort=False).apply(assign_labels)
    return df

def precision_recall_names(df1, df2, dictionary: dict = None):
    """
    We will do precision and recall based on what IS that found
    df1 = ground truth (reference)
    df2 = predictions to evaluate

    TP = df2 locus that matches a df1 locus within buffer
    FP = df2 locus that has no match in df1
    FN = df1 locus that has no match in df2
    """
    tp, fp, fn = 0, 0, 0
    matched_df1 = set()

    # Drop any duplicates in the predicted dataframe
    gt_labels = set(df1.drop_duplicates(subset=["name"]))
    pred_labels = set(df2.drop_duplicates(subset=["IS_label"]))

    # Calculate the TP, FN, FP
    tp_labels = gt_labels & pred_labels
    fn_labels = gt_labels - pred_labels
    fp_labels = pred_labels - gt_labels

    tp, fp, fn = len(tp_labels), len(fp_labels), len(fn_labels)
    precision = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) else 0.0
    recall = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) else 0.0

    summary = {"precision": precision, "recall": recall, "tp": tp, "fp": fp, "fn": fn}

    # actual rows, tagged with their classification
    df2 = df2.copy()
    df2["match_status"] = df2["IS_label"].apply(
        lambda lbl: "TP" if lbl in tp_labels else "FP"

    tp_rows = df2[df2["match_status"] == "TP"]

    fn_rows = df1[df1['name'].isin(fn_labels)]  # ground truth rows that were missed

        "fp_rows": fp_rows,
        "fn_rows": fn_rows,
        "pred_df_tagged": df2,  # full predicted df with match_status column, if you want to inspect everything at once
    }

def locate_subseq(subseq):

Precision, recall and F1
Side: recall is over the truth relations; precision is over eris’s nearest flank on each side (per graph branch). A flank on the wrong side counts as a miss on its true side and a false call on the side reported. Distance: per band (overlapping, near 0–150 bp, far), over relations found on their side. Effect: disrupted only; eris TRUNCATED counts as disrupted.
Recall = TP / (TP + FN) over the truth relations. Precision = TP_calls / (TP_calls + FP) over eris’s calls; for side and effect these are eris’s nearest flanks, so TP_calls can be lower than TP (one collapsed IS locus can find several truth relations, e.g. the flanks of several copies, but has only one nearest flank per side per branch).
